Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to move from our legacy TF-IDF pipeline to an embeddings + rerank architecture for our knowledge search across provider docs and patient-facing help content. A few immediate asks so we can get procurement and engineering lined up: 

- Can you share a proposed backfill strategy for our ~1.2M documents (mix of PDFs, HL7 exports, markdown)? We want to avoid full re-index downtime.
- What vector DBs do you support for a staged migration (we currently use an in-house Faiss cluster but are open to managed services)?
- We need an initial rerank eval plan and signal set so we can prioritize prompt/eval work on our side.
- Any compliance concerns for PII in embeddings generation and retention policy options?

I've attached a short scope spreadsheet with counts and a link to our S3 sample export. Procurement is looped for timeline visibility.

Subject: Re: Embeddings + rerank migration: scope and immediate questions

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the sample export. Short answers up front, details + schedule below.

1) Backfill approach (high level):
   - Stage-gated backfill: seed a small sample index (10k docs) → run rerank evals → progressive bulk backfills in 3 waves (10%, 40%, 50%) with validation gates between each wave.
   - Use prefix/KV caching and read-through during wave 1 to keep cold-start latency down.

2) Vector DB compatibility:
   - Redwood supports Faiss (self-hosted), Milvus, Pinecone, and RedisVector. For your in-house Faiss cluster we can run an adapter + hybrid routing so reads go to Faiss while writes populate a managed replica for fallbacks.

3) Rerank evals:
   - We'll provide a starter eval harness (NDCG@10, MRR, precision@k) and a seed set of 500 labeled queries you can expand. We'll also propose an A/B window for production traffic at 5% → 20% → full.

4) Compliance & retention:
   - Embeddings are reversible only with original text present; we recommend token-redaction rules and configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days). Our Private deployment option supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs if needed.

Attached is a short stage-gated plan PDF and a checklist I want to walk through on the kickoff call. Proposed next steps:
- Kickoff call Thurs 8/12 at 10am PT (30m) to confirm owners and the first-wave sample.
- Marissa to share the initial rerank eval protocol and operational runbook.
- Laura to scope procurement/contracting handoffs and placeholders for SOC2 evidence.

If that works I’ll send invites and a MOP (mutual action plan) draft.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu

Alex / team — adding the runbook skeleton and the rerank eval protocol we’ll use so you can review beforehand. High level of the runbook:

Runbook highlights:
- Wave 0: sample index (10k) — smoke tests, latency profile, rerank A/B at 1% traffic
- Wave 1 (10%): backfill incremental snapshots using high-priority doc tag; validate recall/precision against golden set
- Wave 2 (40%): bulk backfill with parallel workers + throttled ingestion; run distributed re-ranking offline job for cross-validation
- Wave 3 (50%): final cutover and decommission legacy TF-IDF routes; warm caches and monitor token spend

Rerank eval protocol (attached):
- Seed 500 queries with relevance judgments (labels 0/1/2)
- Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, precision@1/5, latency percentiles (p50/p95)
- Regression alert thresholds: >5% drop in NDCG or >100ms p95 latency increase triggers rollback

Ops notes:
- We'll use staged ingestion with checkpoints so we can resume failed workers.
- For Faiss: recommend we snapshot and roll a managed replica against a small vector footprint for the first two waves.

Attaching the protocol for your review. Happy to walk through on the kickoff.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
